promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, 2 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Last week went exactly to plan, and the 17-mile long run felt controlled. This week starts the goal-pace work: an 8-mile session with 4 miles at 8:35 per mile, and an 18-mile long run that finishes at race effort, with no 22-miler needed.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, you do not need a 22-miler before race day. Your 20 on Sep 13 and your 17 on Sep 27 already show the endurance is there.

A 22 at your current pace would take about 3 hours 40 minutes, and the recovery would eat into the sharp days you need before Oct 18. The longest run from here is 18 miles this Sunday, with the last 4 miles at goal pace.

new.analysis:
## The week
Every run from Sep 21 – 27 was done as planned, with each distance within 0.05 miles of the plan and both rest days kept. Nothing was skipped or overrun, and you reported no pain all week.

The Wednesday threshold session was done as written: three 2-mile reps averaging 7:58 per mile, with a 1 percent fade. Heart rate rose from 138 to 157 across it, a normal load for that effort.

Sunday's 17 miles averaged 9:59 per mile at heart rate 146, drifting only 4.7 beats. That tells me the aerobic base is holding well for this distance.

## Next week
Volume rises from 42 to 44 miles, and the midweek medium-long run adds time on feet without a hard day. Two sessions are harder than easy, so your share of time in zones 1 and 2 will sit below 80 percent. That is expected in a week with two quality sessions.

The change this week is intensity, not volume. Goal pace for a 3:45 finish is 8:35 per mile, and the plan now puts it in the Wednesday session and the end of Sunday's run so you practise holding it on tired legs.

## Why 18 and not 22
A 22-miler at your current pace would take about 3 hours 40 minutes. The recovery from that would cut into the sharp days you need in the weeks before the race. Your 20 on Sep 13 and 17 on Sep 27 already show you can handle the time on feet, so the open question is pace control, not distance.

## Pace and heart rate

| Effort | Pace per mile | Heart rate (max 187) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy runs | 9:50 to 10:00 | Under 150 |
| Goal pace (3:45 finish) | 8:35 | About 150 to 155 |
| Threshold reps, Sep 23 | 7:58 average | Averaged 155 |
| Long run, Sep 27 | 9:59 average | Averaged 146 |

Goal pace should feel controlled. If heart rate climbs above 160 early in a block, slow down rather than push to hold pace.

## Taper
The week of Oct 5 – 11 should cut volume noticeably, and race week keeps only short faster running. The work you need is already in this week's plan, so there is no need to add extra running.
